problems.problem:
Over the course of evolution, bacteria have remained small. What are possible explanations for this observation?

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. The cell wall limits the cell volume of bacteria.

B. Lack of compartmentalization limits the cell volume of bacteria.

C. Their small size makes a very high reproduction rate possible.

D. The small size allows faster exchange of substances with the surroundings.

Indicate for each of the following enzymes whether it is involved in eukaryotic DNA replication (true) or not (false).

A. Ligase

B. Primase

C. DNA polymerase

D. Helicase

Order the following molecules by their molecular mass.

A. Lactate (lactic acid) > sucrose > starch > glucose

B. Starch > lactate (lactic acid) > sucrose > glucose

C. Starch > sucrose > glucose > lactate (lactic acid)

D. Starch > glucose > sucrose > lactate (lactic acid)

The figure shows a schematic drawing of a bacterial cell.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2024-1-4-fig1.png

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Structure A consists of a membrane.

B. Part of structure B is made of carbohydrates.

C. Structure C serves for RNA synthesis.

D. Structure D must be in contact with the cytoplasm and the extracellular medium.

The polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is a biochemical method for amplifying DNA in the laboratory.

Indicate for each of the following statements about PCR whether it is true or false.

A. ATP provides the energy for the reaction.

B. At the start of each reaction cycle, the number of DNA molecules is doubled.

C. Primase binds primers to the DNA (primer hybridization).

D. DNA synthesis takes place at 95 °C.

Enzymes are catalysts and accelerate biochemical reactions.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Enzymes are consumed in most biochemical reactions.

B. Enzymes lower the activation energy of a reaction.

C. Enzymes shift the equilibrium towards the products.

D. Enzymes lower the entropy in a system.

Viruses are infectious particles that can multiply only inside living cells.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Viruses use the ribosomes and tRNA molecules of the host cell to synthesize viral proteins.

B. In reverse translation, viral RNA is synthesized using a protein template.

C. DNA viruses must encode a DNA-dependent RNA or DNA polymerase in their genome.

D. RNA viruses must encode an RNA-dependent RNA or DNA polymerase in their genome.

Amanitin is a highly toxic peptide of the death cap mushroom. Even at low concentrations it inhibits RNA polymerase in a highly specific way.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. RNA can no longer be translated.

B. DNA can no longer be transcribed.

C. DNA can no longer be replicated.

D. RNA can no longer be degraded.

The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a membrane system.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. The ER can be connected to the membrane of the nuclear envelope.

B. Inside the ER (the ER lumen), ribosomes synthesize the proteins destined for secretion.

C. The ER lumen is topologically equivalent to the outside of the cell (there is an even number of membranes between the two spaces).

D. The proteins destined for secretion leave the ER via vesicles towards the Golgi apparatus.

In gel electrophoresis, proteins are first denatured (unfolded) and negatively charged, and then migrate along an electric field in a dense gel.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Small proteins migrate through the gel faster than large proteins.

B. With the help of proteins of known masses, the molecular mass of an unknown protein can be determined.

C. Proteins run from the anode (positive pole) towards the cathode (negative pole).

D. A protease can be used to denature proteins for gel electrophoresis.

Sponges are marine, multicellular animals with a simple body plan. It is possible to separate the individual cells of a sponge from one another. If the separated cells are stirred for a while, cell clumps form which can again form a complete sponge. If cells of two different sponge species are mixed, species-specific cell clumps form.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Matching surface structures lead to cell-cell recognition.

B. Lipids in the membrane are decisively involved in clump formation.

C. Membrane proteins and carbohydrates on the membrane surface are decisively involved in clump formation.

D. Cells derived from the same sponge can again form a multicellular tissue.

You stain cells with a staining solution. The cell membrane is permeable to the dye. It diffuses into the cell and stains the cytoplasm.

Which of the following methods do you choose to destain the cells?

A. Rinse the cells repeatedly with water.

B. Place the cells in oil overnight.

C. Place the cells in a highly saline solution overnight.

D. Rinse the cells repeatedly with ethanol.

Indicate for each of the following molecules whether it is transported by the plant tissue shown below in summer (true) or not (false)?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2024-1-13-fig1.png

A. Starch

B. N$_2$

C. H$_2$O

D. CO$_2$

Indicate for each of the following statements about chloroplasts whether it is true or false.

A. New chloroplasts arise by division of existing chloroplasts.

B. Chloroplasts have their own DNA as well as ribosomes.

C. Chloroplasts arose from photosynthetically active yeast fungi that were engulfed by an early eukaryotic cell.

D. In $C_4$ plants, the light reaction takes place in the chloroplasts and the dark reaction in the mitochondria.

The figure shows the result of an experiment in which plant pieces were grown in test tubes with different concentrations of the plant hormones auxin and cytokinin.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2024-1-15-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Kallus = callus; Wurzeln = roots; Spross = shoot; kein Wachstum = no growth; Auxin = auxin; Cytokinin = cytokinin.

Indicate for each of the following statements about the experiment whether it is true or false.

A. Cytokinins are responsible for root growth.

B. A high auxin concentration inhibits all growth.

C. The ratio of the concentrations of the two hormones determines whether a root or a shoot develops.

D. Auxin influences both cell division and cell differentiation.

The maximum height to which trees can grow (approx. 140 m) is largely limited by the transport of water from the roots to the leaves.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Tall trees generally have coarser xylem tissue than small trees.

B. Root pressure counteracts the suction caused by evaporation of water.

C. Water transport in the xylem is mainly passive transport.

D. Tall trees have a high ion concentration in the xylem sap.

Plant cells have some structures that are not present in animal cells.

Indicate for each of the following structures whether it occurs only in plant cells (true) or in plant and animal cells (false).

A. Plasmodesmata

B. Cell membrane

C. Mitochondria

D. Vacuole

Indicate for each of the following statements about photosynthesis whether it is true or false.

A. Carbon fixation is also called the light reaction.

B. The light reaction takes place in the thylakoid membrane.

C. In plants, photosynthesis takes place mainly in the leaf veins.

D. Chloroplasts mainly absorb light in the green region of the spectrum.

Indicate for each of the following statements about nutrient uptake in plants whether it is true or false.

A. Root nodules contain bacteria that release ammonia.

B. Most plants can fix molecular nitrogen (N$_2$) on their own.

C. Plants give energy-rich molecules to mycorrhizal fungi.

D. The cytoplasm of mycorrhizal fungi is directly connected to the cytoplasm of the root cells.

The diagram below shows the anatomical scheme of a flowering plant.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2024-1-20-fig1.png

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Structure D often serves for nutrient storage.

B. Structures A, B and C arose from specialized leaves.

C. The plant shown has an alternate leaf arrangement.

D. Structure B serves for sexual reproduction.

The scanning electron micrograph below shows a specialized plant structure.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2024-1-21-fig1.png

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. This structure serves for water uptake.

B. This structure is called a stoma.

C. This structure is part of the epidermis of trees.

D. The image shows the state of the structure under water shortage.

In type 1 diabetes mellitus, the insulin-producing cells in the pancreas are destroyed by an autoimmune reaction. What symptoms do those affected show?

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. There is an excess of insulin in the blood.

B. The osmolarity of the blood is increased.

C. A urine sample contains a lot of glucose.

D. There is a marked weight gain.

Angiogenesis is the formation and growth of new vessels from existing blood vessels.

In which of the following situations do you expect increased angiogenesis in an adult (true), and in which not (false)?

A. During the menstrual cycle.

B. During muscle growth.

C. During the growth of cancer.

D. During wound healing.

In the kidneys, unwanted substances are filtered out of the blood, while important substances (e.g. proteins) are retained. If proteins are found in the urine, this is called proteinuria.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. A defect of the renal corpuscle can lead to proteinuria.

B. A small amount of protein in the urine is normal.

C. Bleeding in the urethra can lead to proteinuria.

D. Small proteins are retained more readily than large ones.

To digest fats from food, most vertebrates produce bile, which contains bile acids. These are mostly present in conjugated form, as anionic bile salts.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Bile salts are amphiphilic.

B. Without bile, more dietary fat would be excreted.

C. Bile is produced in the gallbladder.

D. Too many bile salts in the intestine cause diarrhea.

Indicate for each of the following statements about the egg cell whether it is true or false.

A. The number of egg cells decreases steadily after birth.

B. In the unfertilized state, egg cells have 23 chromosomes.

C. Egg cells contain a nucleus.

D. During egg cell maturation (oogenesis), four egg cells arise from one precursor cell (oocyte).

The figure below shows the uptake of glucose from the intestinal contents via the intestinal epithelial cells into the blood.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2024-1-27-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Glukose = glucose; Fruktose = fructose.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Without a sodium gradient, glucose uptake is still possible.

B. Both GLUT2 and GLUT5 allow transport against a gradient.

C. The sodium-potassium ATPase transports sodium ions out of the cell into the blood.

D. Glucose uptake from the intestine takes place by diffusion.

The figure below shows a sarcomere of a muscle in the electron microscope and as a diagram.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2024-1-28-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Z-Linie = Z line; M-Bande = M band; H-Zone = H zone; I-Bande = I band; A-Bande = A band.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. The Z line becomes wider when the muscle contracts.

B. A sarcomere consists of two half I bands and one A band.

C. The A band contains only actin.

D. When the muscle contracts, the A band shortens.

Invertebrates have an innate but no adaptive immune system.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. On reinfection with the same pathogen, the immune response of invertebrates is faster.

B. If invertebrates grow up in a sterile environment, they are more susceptible to disease.

C. Invertebrates have phagocytes.

D. Invertebrates have specific antibodies.

The following figure shows the normal course of an action potential. During an action potential, voltage-gated sodium channels open and the cell is depolarized by an influx of Na$^+$ into the cell. After the action potential has taken place, the sodium channels close again.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2024-1-30-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Membranpotential = membrane potential; Depolarisation = depolarization; Repolarisation = repolarization; Schwellenpotential = threshold potential; Ruhepotential = resting potential; Hyperpolarisation = hyperpolarization; Reiz = stimulus.

The poison of the pufferfish prevents the opening of voltage-gated sodium channels in neurons. What do you expect as a consequence?

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. The muscles become paralyzed.

B. Sodium ions flow out of the cell uncontrollably.

C. No action potential can be triggered any more.

D. The membrane potential becomes ever more positive.

The diagram shows the regulation of the thyroid hormones. TSH stimulates the thyroid cells to produce T3 and T4. For the thyroid to be able to produce T3 and T4, enough iodine is needed.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2024-1-31-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Hypophyse = pituitary gland; Schilddrüse = thyroid gland; Iod = iodine.

What happens if we take in too little iodine?

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. We measure increased TSH levels.

B. The T3 and T4 produced contain less iodine.

C. The thyroid cells can produce less T3 and T4.

D. The hypothalamus produces less TRH.

Indicate for each of the following assignments between circulatory system and animal whether it is correct (true) or not (false).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2024-1-32-fig1.png

A. Vespa crabro (hornet)

B. Carcharodon carcharias (great white shark)

C. Phyllobates terribilis (poison dart frog)

D. Falco peregrinus (peregrine falcon)

Indicate for each of the following statements about the circulatory systems from the question above whether it is true or false.

A. Animals with circulation type C are adapted to sustained high endurance performance.

B. Mammalian embryos have circulation type C, while adult animals have circulation type D.

C. Oxygenated blood is on the left side in the diagram.

D. A and C are examples of open circulatory systems.

Indicate for each of the following statements about blood flow in the heart whether it is true or false.

A. Blood enters the right half of the heart via the pulmonary veins.

B. The pulmonary arteries are the starting point of the systemic circulation.

C. The atrioventricular (cuspid) valves are open when blood is pumped into the pulmonary circulation.

D. The pulmonary arteries carry deoxygenated blood.

An edema is an accumulation of fluid outside the blood vessels. Various mechanisms contribute to the exchange of fluid between the vessels and the tissue:

• Hydrostatic pressure (pressure of the fluid inside the vessels)
• Oncotic pressure (pressure that draws water towards the proteins in the vessels)
• The permeability of the vessels
• Lymphatic drainage (filtrate from the blood plasma)

Indicate for each of the following mechanisms whether it could cause an edema (true) or not (false).

A. Decrease in the permeability of the vessels

B. Increase in hydrostatic pressure

C. Increase in oncotic pressure

D. Decrease in lymphatic drainage

Indicate for each of the following statements about digestion in mammals whether it is true or false.

A. The spleen produces digestive enzymes.

B. The main function of the large intestine is the absorption of water and electrolytes.

C. Protein digestion begins in the mouth.

D. The enzymes needed for starch digestion are secreted in the stomach.

You observe a population of a certain animal species and after some time notice that some individuals of the population do not produce offspring themselves but instead help other individuals to care for their offspring.

Indicate for each of the following characteristics whether you expect it in this animal species (true) or not (false).

A. Close kinship between the helpers and those helped

B. Very high birth rate

C. Elaborate care of the offspring

D. Stable social structures

Since 2020, attacks by killer whales (Orcinus orca) have been observed in which the animals (alone or in groups) ram boats and attack their rudders. At first this behavior occurred only off the Spanish and Portuguese coasts, but meanwhile it seems to be spreading from there into northern waters. Several boats have been sunk, but there have never been any human fatalities.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Attacks in groups are an example of altruistic behavior.

B. This behavior is instinctive behavior.

C. With this behavior, the killer whales open up a new food source.

D. This behavior probably spreads by social learning.

In behavioral biology, the term imprinting refers to an irreversible form of learning that takes place during a genetically determined period in response to a particular stimulus.

Indicate for each of the following examples whether the behavior can be explained by the principle of imprinting (true) or not (false).

A. Pavlov's dog produces saliva in anticipation of food when a bell rings.

B. Blue jays that had to vomit after eating monarch butterflies avoid eating butterflies that look similar to monarch butterflies.

C. Newly hatched greylag geese identify an object that moves away from them as their mother.

D. Young chimpanzees learn, by observing conspecifics, how to crack nuts with two stones.

The coefficient of relatedness gives the average proportion of identical alleles between individuals.

Indicate for the following combinations of species and coefficients of relatedness between biological sisters (same parents) whether they match (true) or not (false).

A. Aequorea victoria (crystal jelly) => 100 %

B. Felis silvestris (wildcat) => 50 %

C. Formica rufa (red wood ant) => 75 %

D. Rhincodon typus (whale shark) => 25 %

The plumage of a bird species is colored either green or blue. We assume that the color is determined by one gene, with green being dominant and blue recessive.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. If the birds mate randomly and there is no natural selection, the blue individuals die out after some time.

B. If two homozygous individuals of different color mate, all offspring are green.

C. If two green birds mate, all their offspring are green.

D. At least one parent of a green bird is green.

Indicate for each of the following statements about reproduction whether it is true or false.

A. Asexual reproduction leads to greater genetic diversity than sexual reproduction.

B. Conifers are able to reproduce sexually.

C. Sexual selection occurs only with sexual reproduction.

D. To reproduce asexually, meiosis must be carried out.

Oculocutaneous albinism type II is an autosomal recessive hereditary disease.

Assuming that on average one in 10,000 people is affected by this disease, how large is the proportion of healthy carriers in this population?

A. 10 %

B. 2 %

C. 1 %

D. 20 %

What is the probability that a randomly chosen 2-base-pair sequence in the human genome has the sequence "AG"?

A. 6.25%

B. 25%

C. 32.25%

D. 0%

Overo spotting is a coat color of the horse characterized by broad, irregular white patches on a darker coat. Analysis of the gene responsible for overo spotting shows that all spotted individuals are heterozygous for this gene.

Which is the most likely explanation for this phenomenon?

A. The gene is homozygous lethal.

B. It is mitochondrial inheritance.

C. Heterozygous individuals have higher chances of survival.

D. There was a point mutation in the gene.

Epigenetics studies phenomena that lead to changes in gene expression without changes in the DNA sequence. In eukaryotic cells, DNA methylation (the attachment of a methyl group to certain bases of the DNA) reduces the activity of genes by preventing their transcription.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Methylation of a tumor suppressor gene could lead to the development of cancer.

B. Methylation prevents transcription factors from binding to the DNA.

C. You expect the hemoglobin gene to be demethylated in blood cells.

D. The methylation of genes is maintained during embryonic development.

The graph below shows the genomic diversity of elephant populations as a function of distance from Botswana.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2024-1-47-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Genomische Diversität = genomic diversity; Distanz zu Botswana = distance from Botswana.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Elephants probably arose several times independently of one another from an ancestral species.

B. In the populations farther from Botswana, founder effects probably played a role.

C. Elephants show pronounced migratory behavior.

D. Genomic diversity correlates negatively with distance from Botswana.

Which of the following evolutionary innovations is the oldest?

A. Gills

B. Multicellularity

C. ATP synthase

D. Cell nucleus

In a population that is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, the dominant allele A has a frequency of 30%.

How frequent are individuals with genotype AA?

A. 9%

B. 42%

C. 49%

D. 70%

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2024-1-50-fig1.png

Which mode of inheritance most likely applies to this disease?

A. X-linked dominant

B. Autosomal dominant

C. Autosomal recessive

D. X-linked recessive

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2024-1-51-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Amazonas-Flussdelfine = Amazon river dolphins; Delfine = dolphins; Ganges-Indus-Flussdelfine = Ganges and Indus river dolphins; Pottwale = sperm whales.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false based on the information in the tree.

A. River dolphins evolved from oceanic dolphins only once.

B. The tree was probably constructed on the basis of gill morphologies.

C. The dolphins that formerly lived in Switzerland form a monophyletic group.

D. The dolphins that formerly lived in Switzerland were exclusively freshwater dolphins.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. An organism can belong to several genera at the same time.

B. All unicellular organisms together form a monophyletic group.

C. All known living organisms probably descend from a common ancestor.

D. The dandelion is more closely related to the Norway spruce than to a fern.

Indicate for each of the following statements about the different species concepts whether it is true or false.

A. The morphological species concept is based on the observation of individuals and their characteristics.

B. The biological species concept is often the most useful species concept for bacteria.

C. Of all systematic groupings, natural selection acts only on the species.

D. According to the biological species concept, horses and donkeys belong to the same species.

In the mid-1990s, studies showed that a subpopulation of the common pipistrelle (Pipistrellus pipistrellus) is actually a separate species, the soprano pipistrelle (Pipistrellus pygmaeus).

What is the most likely reason for this reclassification of the subpopulation?

A. The genes of the subpopulation are not identical to those of the common pipistrelles.

B. The subpopulation cannot produce viable offspring with the common pipistrelles.

C. The subpopulation lives in a different habitat.

D. The subpopulation has a lighter fur color and more aggressive behavior.

In a backcross, an individual is crossed with a partner that is homozygous for a recessive allele.

Indicate for each of the following statements about backcrosses whether it is true or false.

A. With codominant inheritance, no conclusion about the genotype of the individual can be drawn from the phenotypes of the offspring.

B. If the phenotype of 4 offspring is determined, the genotype of the individual can be determined unambiguously from this.

C. If the individual tested is heterozygous, all offspring show the dominant phenotype.

D. If the individual tested is homozygous, the offspring have phenotypes in a ratio of 3:1.

Consider the food chain shown. Due to warmer and more favorable climatic conditions, the supply of grasses increases over several years.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2024-1-56-fig1.png

Indicate for each of the following effects whether it will probably occur under these conditions (true) or not (false).

A. The reproduction rate of the rabbits increases.

B. The rabbit population decreases.

C. The least weasels no longer hunt rabbits.

D. The long-eared owl population increases.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. The relationship between lions and antelopes is an example of commensalism.

B. The relationship between mistletoe and a tree is an example of parasitism.

C. The relationship between bees and flowering plants is an example of mutualism.

D. The relationship between ants and acacias is an example of symbiosis.

Indicate for each of the following statements about ecological niches whether it is true or false.

A. The sudden appearance of a new ecological niche leads to speciation.

B. Two species with an identical ecological niche are in competition.

C. The fundamental ecological niche is always larger than the realized ecological niche.

D. A species with a broad ecological niche is more competitive.

In the forest you observe three snake species with similar, conspicuous coloration. One is harmless, one is mildly venomous and the third is highly venomous (lethal).

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Highly venomous snakes that have the same coloration as mildly venomous snakes have an evolutionary advantage.

B. Non-venomous snakes that have the same coloration as mildly venomous snakes have an evolutionary advantage.

C. The non-venomous snake is a parasite.

D. The coloration of the snakes is probably a homologous trait.

Over a long period you observe a flower species that occurs both on the mainland and on a remote island and is pollinated by a hummingbird. After some time you observe that the flowers on the island are markedly longer and, at the same time, the hummingbirds have a markedly longer bill.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. This is an example of coevolution.

B. If this trend continues, this could be an example of sympatric speciation.

C. The hummingbirds with a longer bill would also have a competitive advantage on the mainland.

D. This fact is based on a bottleneck effect (bottle neck).

In ecology, species are distinguished by their reproductive strategy. K-strategists have few offspring, in which they invest a lot of time. In contrast, r-strategists have many offspring, in which they invest little or no time.

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. The dandelion is a K-strategist.

B. In r-strategists, high mortality among young individuals is expected.

C. K-strategists have an advantage when environmental conditions are very variable.

D. K-strategists tend to be found at higher trophic levels.

Indicate for each of the following cell components whether it is present in a prokaryotic cell (true) or not (false).

A. Cell wall

B. Chloroplasts

C. Nucleus

D. Ribosomes

Indicate for each of the following statements about viruses whether it is true or false.

A. Viruses can only replicate in a living host cell.

B. Viruses carry out cellular respiration to obtain energy.

C. Viruses can only infect eukaryotic cells.

D. Viruses possess genetic material made of DNA or RNA.

A. The equilibrium of the reaction shown lies on the side of the product.

The polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is an enzymatic reaction in which double-stranded DNA is duplicated.

Indicate for each of the following molecules or groups of molecules whether you would expect it in a PCR reaction (true) or not (false).

A. Heat-stable polymerase

B. ATP

C. Single-stranded DNA

D. mRNA

Indicate for each of the following processes whether it takes place in the nucleus of a eukaryotic cell (true) or not (false).
